title: Rate policy backpressure during edge rebalance causes transient over-throttles and missing metering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During planned and unplanned edge shard rebalances the rate-policy backpressure signals can be applied out-of-order and with stale state to shard-local enforcers. The result is a short window where some keys are aggressively throttled (double-enforced) while their meter increments are dropped or delayed, causing both user-facing latency/throttles and undercounted usage for billing. This ticket drives diagnosis, short-term mitigation, and a robust fix.

Why it matters: customer-facing throttles for active keys + undercounted metering = incorrect SLA behavior and potential billing variance. We observed this during a geo-rebalance yesterday and have one on-call report from a high-usage customer complaining about elevated 429s and missing line items in billing exports.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a two-shard edge pool and enable per-route hierarchical policies with burst credits and grace windows.
2) Drive high, sustained traffic from a single API key that will be split across shards during rebalance (simulate by toggling shard weights).
3) Trigger a rebalance (scale-down one shard or issue manual shard-move) while traffic is active.

4) Observe that enforcer A receives a backpressure broadcast and applies a local cooldown; enforcer B receives a delayed cancel and applies overlapping backpressure leading to double-throttle on the same key.
5) Check metering ingestion stream: some meter events originating from the briefly-throttled path are missing or delayed by >30s.
Expected: consistent allow/deny decision across shards with no loss of meter increments during rebalance.
observations: - Reproducible in staging with a scripted rebalance (100% when using small rebalance interval).
- Traces show duplicate policy-eval messages, then an out-of-order expiry event that causes sticky cooldown on the wrong shard for ~7-20s.
- Metering log consumer shows a gap in events correlated to the time window of the double-throttle; the producer path retries but commits are deduplicated/missed during shard handoff.
- Backpressure messages currently rely on a best-effort pub/sub with no causal ordering and no per-key epoch stamping.
hypothesis: Root cause is a combination of: (a) lack of monotonic epoch/version per-key when broadcasting backpressure; (b) short anti-entropy missing between enforcer handoff and meter flush; (c) local enforcers applying cooldowns that are not reversible when newer state arrives due to idempotency gaps.
Secondary contributor: meter producer buffers are dropped during graceful shutdown and not fully drained before shard claim transfer.
proposed_short_term_mitigations: 1) Disable aggressive cooldowns on backpressure events during an active rebalance window (feature flag runtime.disable_aggressive_cooldown).
2) Increase meter-producer drain timeout from 2s -> 15s during shard shutdown to reduce lost increments (configurable).
3) Add a temporary reconciliation job to replay missed meter events from producer logs into the billing pipeline for the incident window.
4) Notify affected customers and add credits where appropriate while fix is deployed.
proposed_long_term_fix: - Introduce per-key monotonic epochs for policy broadcasts: every broadcast includes key_epoch and sequence, enforcers ignore stale epochs.
- Make cooldown application idempotent and reversible: cooldowns must carry expiry and origin_epoch; newer epochs can cancel older cooldowns atomically.
- Implement a handoff handshake: when a shard transfer occurs, the old owner performs a synchronous drain+handoff of outstanding meter batches for keys being migrated (best-effort with retries).
- Add anti-entropy pass in the enforcer reconciler that verifies local counters against global aggregator every 30s for recently-moved keys and emits fixup meter events if delta > threshold.
acceptance_criteria: - In staging, scripted rebalance no longer produces overlapping double-throttles for the same key (observed allow/deny decisions consistent across shards).
- Metering ingestion gaps observed before are eliminated in a repeatable test (no missing events beyond normal retry window).
- Performance impact: added epoch metadata and handshake adds <1% p50 latency to policy evals in benchmarked tests.
- Rollout plan and feature flags exist for the aggressive cooldown toggle and increased drain timeout.
- Post-deploy runbook for monitoring: per-key rebalancing counters, stale-epoch rejects, and meter-replay alerts instrumented in console.
work_log: 2026-03-12: Aisha created ticket after PagerDuty alert and initial blameless postmortem notes. Linked to customer's support thread and billing export snapshot.
2026-03-12: Marco reproduced failure in staging with small-pool rebalance script; captured traces and prepared flamegraphs. (see /artifacts/staging/rebalance-traces-0312.tar.gz)
2026-03-13: Infra added temporary feature flag runtime.disable_aggressive_cooldown=true in staging; observed immediate reduction in double-throttles but meter gaps remained.
2026-03-13: Billing lead (Sofia Nguyen) requested a reconciliation of customer invoices while we investigate. Temporary credit agreed for affected customers.
2026-03-14: Prototype epoch-stamping added to broadcast layer (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/kl/epoch-backpressure-proto). Initial unit tests passing.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Increasing drain timeout reduces event loss risk but increases overall shard shutdown time and may delay autoscaling responsiveness.
- Adding epochs increases per-message size and enforcer CPU parsing cost; must measure overhead across high-throughput clusters.
- Synchronous handoff introduces a blocking path on shard transfer; we must mitigate with backoff and fallbacks.
next_steps: 1) Ship short-term mitigations behind flags to production canary (Marco + Infra).
2) Extend benchmark suite to include epoch metadata and measure p50/p95 impact (Perf team).
3) Implement and test epoch-based broadcasts and idempotent cooldown semantics (ENG runtime team).
4) Prepare billing reconciliation utility and run it for the incident window (Billing + SRE).
5) Draft runbook and monitoring dashboards for post-deploy validation (SRE + Console).
